# The Interval Trainer release signing certificate: SHA-256 over the DER-encoded
# certificate — the same value `keytool -list -v` prints as `SHA256:` (in
# uppercase, colon-separated) and apksigner prints as
# "certificate SHA-256 digest" (bare lowercase hex). Pinned here by issue #10
# so a release APK signed by any other key fails its job before it is published.
#
# This is PUBLIC data. It ships inside every APK, so anyone holding a release
# build already has it; committing it in the clear is what lets a gate check a
# build without being handed anything that could sign one. The keystore and its
# passwords are the secrets, and they live only as the repository secrets
# ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 / ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD / ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS /
# ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS_PASSWORD. Nothing that unlocks the key belongs in this file
# or anywhere else in this repository.
#
# It must never change. A different fingerprint here means a different signing
# key, and Android will not install a differently-signed APK over an installed
# one: every user would have to uninstall first, destroying the app's data.
# There is no key recovery for a sideloaded app. See
# docs/adr/0001-release-signing-with-a-stable-keystore.md.
2f596b227b890f5fcec72c176f0e325623e6261f00ddb102c4f936e9da108e09
